messages:
maria: heads up, ALB started deregistering a bunch of edge targets in eu-west-1 at ~03:05 UTC. Healthcheck RTTs spiked from ~20ms to 400-600ms intermittently and targets flip to UNHEALTHY (Timeout). Pods show Ready. Any correlation with recent node/nodepool changes or NAT churn?

aj: seeing it too. ALB TargetHealth reports "Timeout" not 5xx. Pod readiness probes are green. My hunch: return path is getting broken by SNAT port churn — ephemeral port reuse after a burst of outbound connections (model downloads / telemetry). ALB healthcheck packets likely get mismatched replies.

kyler: fyi we triggered a nodepool autoscaler and GPU onboarding at 02:58 in that AZ — that caused ENI attachments and some egress ip reassignment. Could be NAT affinity rotation.

maria: collecting quick evidence — ALB access log sample and conntrack on one failing node:

ALB log (partial):
alblog: 2026-03-18T03:05:12Z target:10.0.45.12:8080 elb_status:504 target_status:- response_time:0.602
alblog: 2026-03-18T03:05:19Z target:10.0.45.12:8080 elb_status:200 target_status:200 response_time:0.023

on node-uk-edge-12:
$ sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.0.45.12 | tail -n 6
udp 17 src=10.0.45.12 dst=34.213.44.78 sport=34567 dport=31943 ... TIME_WAIT
udp 17 src=10.0.45.12 dst=34.213.44.78 sport=34568 dport=31943 ... TIME_WAIT
(tons of ephemeral ports in WAIT)

aj: repro steps I ran: curl from ALB to pod endpoint (via target registered ip) succeeds, then immediately after an outbound burst from pod to S3/GCS the next curl times out. Looks like client source port mapping changed / reply went to different NAT mapping.

kyler: deploy-bot: nodepool-rollout finished at 02:59 (no errors).

deploy-bot: nodepool-rollout completed for gpu-pool-eu-west-1-a at 02:59:21 UTC.

sre-oncall: opening incident: INC-2026-0459 — marking as P1 for now. Short-term mitigations: 1) increase ALB healthcheck timeout and interval slack, 2) temporarily increase pod readiness probe timeout to avoid flapping, 3) add a small set of static egress IPs for edge pods to reduce SNAT churn.

aj: quick mitigation patch I can push: readiness.probe.timeoutSeconds -> 15, probe.periodSeconds -> 10 for edge deployment; also set HTTP keepalive on outbound clients to reduce ephemeral churn. I'll push a canary.

kyler: long-term: we should consider NAT IP pool resizing per nodepool scale events or use EIP per ENI for edge nodes, and investigate conntrack/tcp_tw_recycle style tuning (careful). Also look at iptables hashlimit or firewall rules that might drop healthcheck packets when conntrack tables spike.

maria: action items: 1) aj to push probe timeout canary in eu-west-1 (in flight), 2) kyler to investigate egress IP persistence options and open infra ticket, 3) sre-oncall to add temporary ALB healthcheck slack and incident doc. I'll monitor for 30m and report. :eyes: 

aj: canary rolling now to 5 pods in canary ASG. will update in 5m. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: INC-2026-0459 created: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0459 — adding timeline and owner tags.

maria: thanks — if we still see flaps after canary, we'll revert and try proving the egress IP hypothesis with tcpdump on node before next scale event.
